arxiv-2208-02696.title: Axion-like particles from primordial black hole evaporation and their detection in neutrino experiments
arxiv-2208-02696.creator: Tong Li, Rui-Jia Zhang
arxiv-2208-02696.description: Abstract The primordial black holes (PBHs) play as a novel source to radiate light elementary particles of energies in the region of a few hundred MeV. We explore the possibility that the light axion-like particles (ALPs) are produced from PBH evaporation.

arxiv-2209-07782.title: Localization of the Kobayashi distance for any visibility domain Thanks: The author is supported by the postdoctoral fellowship of Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Kolkata.
arxiv-2209-07782.creator: Amar Deep Sarkar
arxiv-2209-07782.description: Abstract . In this article, we prove localization results for the Kobayashi distance of Kobayashi hyperbolic domains with local visibility property in ℂ d \mathbb{C}^{d} , d ≥ 1 d\geq 1 . This is done by proving a localization result for the Kobayashi-Royden pseudometric, along with some other results for domains satisfying local weak visibility.

arxiv-2305-15348.title: READ: Recurrent Adaptation of Large Transformers
arxiv-2305-15348.creator: John Nguyen Sid Wang Ke Li Carole-Jean Wu
arxiv-2305-15348.description: Abstract In the realm of Natural Language Processing (NLP), large-scale transformers have established themselves as pivotal, achieving unparalleled results across numerous tasks. The conventional approach involves pre-training these models on extensive web-scale data, followed by fine-tuning them for specific downstream tasks.

arxiv-2307-05659.title: Probing the Quantitative–Qualitative Divide in Probabilistic Reasoning
arxiv-2307-05659.creator: Duligur Ibeling, Thomas Icard
arxiv-2307-05659.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Duligur Ibeling, Thomas Icard. This paper explores the space of (propositional) probabilistic logical languages, ranging from a purely ‘qualitative’ comparative language to a highly ‘quantitative’ language involving arbitrary polynomials over probability terms. While talk of qualitative vs. quantitative may be suggestive, we identify a robust and meaningful boundary in the space by distinguishing systems that encode (at most) additive reasoning from those that encode additive and multiplicative reasoning.

arxiv-2307-11834.title: General relativistic pulsations of ultra-massive ZZ Ceti stars 2023 General relativistic pulsations of ultra-massive ZZ Ceti stars – 2
arxiv-2307-11834.creator: Alejandro H. Córsico, S. Reece Boston, Leandro G. Althaus, Mukremin Kilic, S. O. Kepler, María E. Camisassa, Santiago Torres
arxiv-2307-11834.description: Abstract Ultra-massive white dwarf stars are currently being discovered at a considerable rate, thanks to surveys such as the Gaia space mission. These dense and compact stellar remnants likely play a major role in type Ia supernova explosions. It is possible to probe the interiors of ultra-massive white dwarfs through asteroseismology.

arxiv-2403-07625.title: Identifying a point-symmetric morphology in supernova remnant Cassiopeia A: explosion by jittering jets
arxiv-2403-07625.creator: Ealeal Bear, Noam Soker
arxiv-2403-07625.description: Abstract We identify a point-symmetric morphology of the supernova remnant (SNR) Cassiopeia A compatible with shaping by at least two, and more likely more than four, pairs of opposite jets, as expected in the jittering jets explosion mechanism (JJEM) of core-collapse supernovae.

arxiv-2407-17578.title: Neutron stars as extreme gravity probes
arxiv-2407-17578.creator: Hector O. Silva
arxiv-2407-17578.description: Abstract Neutron stars are powerful probes into the extremes of physics. In this chapter, we will discuss how observations of neutron stars, either in isolation or in binaries, can be leveraged to test general relativity and constrain competing theories of gravity. Note added in the arXiv version: this text reflects the subject’s status as of January 16th, 2024.

arxiv-2505-09246.title: Focus, Merge, Rank: Improved Question Answering Based on Semi-Structured Knowledge Bases
arxiv-2505-09246.creator: Derian Boer \orcid 0000-0002-2304-6613, Stephen Roth, Stefan Kramer \orcid 0000-0003-0136-2540
arxiv-2505-09246.description: Abstract In many real-world settings, machine learning models and interactive systems have access to both structured knowledge, e.g., knowledge graphs or tables, and unstructured content, e.g., natural language documents. However, most rely on either. Semi-Structured Knowledge Bases (SKBs) bridge this gap by linking unstructured content to nodes within structured data, thereby enabling new strategies for knowledge access and use.

arxiv-2505-16220.title: Meta-PerSER: Few-Shot Listener Personalized Speech Emotion Recognition via Meta-learning
arxiv-2505-16220.creator: Liang-Yeh, Shi-Xin, Yi-Cheng, Huang-Cheng, Hung-yi
arxiv-2505-16220.description: Abstract This paper introduces Meta-PerSER , a novel meta-learning framework that personalizes Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) by adapting to each listener’s unique way of interpreting emotion. Conventional SER systems rely on aggregated annotations, which often overlook individual subtleties and lead to inconsistent predictions.

arxiv-2506-12216.creator: Vladimir G. Ushakov, Emile S. Medvedev
arxiv-2506-12216.description: Abstract The line list for the principal isotopologue of CO calculated earlier by the present authors Medvedev22preprint , Medvedev22 with the irregular dipole-moment function (DMF) is updated with use of the recent high-precision measurements in the 3-0 Bielska22 , Hodges25 (Bielska et al. 2022, Hodges et al. 2025) and 7-0 Balashov23 (Balashov et al. 2023) bands.

pmc-12507490.title: Symptomatic Postoperative Pneumocephalus: A Case Series and Review of Management Strategies
pmc-12507490.creator: Chris Marcellino, Christopher Koo
pmc-12507490.description: Postoperative (or postprocedural) pneumocephalus is unique from those associated with head injury, spontaneous cerebrospinal fluid leaks, and intracranial infection. pmc-13259633.title: The relationship of forage intake, residual feed intake, and greenhouse gas emissions between lactation and gestation in beef cows
pmc-13259633.creator: Samuel R Talley, Emma A Briggs, Bailey J Tomson, Mariana E Garcia-Ascolani, Paul A Beck, R Ryan Reuter, Andrew P Foote, Megan M Rolf, David L Lalman
pmc-13259633.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The objective of this research was to evaluate dry matter intake (DMI), residual feed intake (RFI), and greenhouse gas emissions between lactation and gestation in mature beef cows fed an unprocessed grass hay diet. A two-year experiment was conducted using 67 mature Angus and Angus-cross cows (n = 41, Year 1; n = 26, Year 2) which included a minimum 85-d early-mid lactation trial (LACT) followed by a minimum 85-d early-mid gestation trial (GEST) in both years.

pmc-13512387.creator: Daniel Markthaler, Kai Peter Birke
pmc-13512387.description: The Ising model provides a fundamental setting for investigating the emergence of phase transitions from simple interacting degrees of freedom. The current characterization study serves to investigate central requirements for phase transitions in terms of connectivity, i.e., the degree of coupled interactions between interaction sites.
